name: Fibre-pigtailed micropillar quantum-dot single-photon source operated at 2.4 K in a compact closed-cycle Gifford-McMahon cryocooler
plain_name: Run a fibre-connected single-photon light source inside a compact refrigerator
description: Attach a single-mode UHNA3 fibre to an electrically contacted (reverse-biased, Stark-tuned) micropillar quantum-dot source, cool it in a compact two-stage GM cryocooler to 2.4 K, excite it with shaped 79.21 MHz pulses and measure brightness, g2(0) and indistinguishability through the fibre over many hours and thermal cycles.
keywords: Run a fibre-connected single-photon light source inside a compact refrigerator

sources.citation: Efficient fibre-pigtailed source of indistinguishable single photons (Margaria et al., Nature Communications 16, 7553, 2025)

reported_equipment: femtosecond laser with a repetition rate of 79.21 MHz

requirements.rationale: The pigtailed source was operated at the 2.4 K base temperature of the cryocooler.
The purpose of the procedure is operation in compact closed-cycle cryocoolers without liquid cryogens.
Excitation and collection run through a single-mode fibre feedthrough to the pigtailed device.
The micropillar is electrically contacted and reverse-biased to stabilise the charge state and Stark-tune the emission by more than 150 pm.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
